2019 El Paso Walmart shooting: United States. On August 3, 2019, a mass shooting occurred at a Walmart store in El Paso, Texas, United States.

Chera dynasty: India. The Chera country was geographically well placed at the tip of the Indian peninsula to profit from maritime trade via the extensive Indian Ocean networks.

Which country uses the grivna as its official currency?

Ahmadiyya is an Islamic messianic movement originating in British India in the late 19th century.

Amit Shah (born 22 October 1964) is an Indian politician who has served as the 31st Minister of Home Affairs since 2019, the longest-serving holder of the office in Indian history.

This 19th-century Habsburg-Lorraine royal fathered two emperors — one who ruled from Vienna, the other who ruled Mexico — and was grandfather to the royal whose 1914 assassination triggered World War I — who is he?
Archduke Franz Karl of Austria (17 December 1802 - 8 March 1878) was a member of the House of Habsburg-Lorraine.

This Swedish diplomat became the youngest person ever elected UN Secretary-General at just 47, serving from 1953 until his death in a 1961 plane crash — who is he?

Dag Hammarskjöld (29 July 1905 - 18 September 1961) was a Swedish economist and diplomat who served as the second Secretary-General of the United Nations from April 1953 until his death in a plane crash in September 1961.
Nominated three times for the Medal of Honor and finally awarded it for his WWII service in the Philippines, this American general also served as Army chief of staff in the 1930s. Who is he?
Douglas MacArthur (26 January 1880 - 5 April 1964) was an American general who served as a top commander during World War II and the Korean War, achieving the rank of General of the Army.

A World War I officer decorated with the Pour le Mérite, he later wrote the tactics classic 'Infantry Attacks' and commanded the 7th Panzer Division — though history remembers him as 'The Desert Fox.' Who was he?
Erwin Rommel (15 November 1891 - 14 October 1944), known as The Desert Fox, was a German Generalfeldmarschall (field marshal) during World War II.
This Norse goddess of love, beauty, and war owns a magical necklace called Brísingamen, rides a chariot pulled by two cats, and can transform into a falcon using an enchanted cloak — who is she?
Freyja (Old Norse '(the) Lady') is a goddess associated with love, beauty, fertility, sex, war, gold, and seir (magic for seeing and influencing the future).
Founded in 918, this Korean kingdom achieved what historians call the peninsula's first true national unification, ruling until the Joseon dynasty was established in 1392 — what kingdom was it?

Goryeo (Middle) was a Korean state founded in 918, during a time of national division called the Later Three Kingdoms period, that unified and ruled the Korean Peninsula until the establishment of Joseon in 1392.
Often depicted holding twin torches or a key, or accompanied by dogs, this Greek goddess of crossroads, magic, and witchcraft first appeared in Hesiod's Theogony in the 8th century BCE — who is she?

Hecate (Ancient) is a goddess in ancient Greek religion and mythology, most often shown holding a pair of torches, a key, or snakes, or accompanied by dogs, and in later periods depicted as three-formed or triple-bodied.

Descended from a Welsh noble family and Catherine of Valois, this English and Welsh royal dynasty held the throne from 1485 to 1603 across five monarchs including Henry VIII and Elizabeth I — name the dynasty?
House of Tudor was an English and Welsh dynasty that held the throne of England from 1485 to 1603.
This Israeli far-right politician has served as minister of national security since 2022 and leads a Kahanist party called 'Jewish Power.' Who is he?
Itamar Ben-Gvir (born 6 May 1976) is an Israeli politician and lawyer who has served as the minister of national security since 2022, except for a two-month gap in early 2025.
This California politician served two non-consecutive stints as governor decades apart, making him both the state's oldest and, at the time, its sixth-youngest governor — who is he?
Jerry Brown (born April 7, 1938) is an American lawyer, author, and politician who served as the 34th and 39th governor of California from 1975 to 1983 and 2011 to 2019.
Overthrown in 1955 yet returned to Argentina's presidency in 1973, this military-college graduate gave his name to a political force still shaping the country — who?

Juan Perón (8 October 1895 - 1 July 1974) was an Argentine military officer and politician who was the 29th and 40th president of Argentina, serving from 1946 to his overthrow in 1955, and from 1973 until his death in 1974.

Founded around 1000 AD when Stephen I was crowned its first king, this Central European monarchy — later split by Ottoman occupation into three parts — endured for nearly a millennium until 1946. What was it?
Kingdom of Hungary was a monarchy in Central Europe that existed for nearly a millennium, from 1000 to 1946.

This US Army officer served with the 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment of the 101st Airborne during World War II, and was portrayed by Ron Livingston in the HBO miniseries Band of Brothers — who is he?

Quoted by Jesus in 'You cannot serve both God and ___,' this New Testament word for wealth was later personified in medieval tradition as one of the seven princes of Hell, representing greed — what's the word?
Mammon is commonly thought to mean money, material wealth, or any entity that promises wealth, and is associated with the greedy pursuit of gain.
This American memoirist and poet's first of seven autobiographies, published in 1969, told of her life up to age 17 and brought her international recognition. Who is she?

Known as "The Proclamator," this independence activist was once jailed in the Boven Digoel concentration camp before becoming his country's very first vice president. Who was he?

Mohammad Hatta (n Athar; 12 August 1902 - 14 March 1980) was an Indonesian statesman, nationalist, and independence activist who served as the country's first vice president as well as the third prime minister.

Most often used as an insult and rarely pinned to one clear definition, this late-20th-century ideology champions free-market capitalism through lower taxes, privatization and deregulation — what is it called?
Neoliberalism is a political and economic ideology that advocates for free-market capitalism, which became dominant in policy-making from the late 20th century onward.
According to Genesis, this second son of Judah defied the custom of levirate marriage with his brother Er's widow, Tamar, and was punished for it — who was he?
Onan was a figure detailed in the Book of Genesis chapter 38, as the second son of Judah and his Canaanite wife, the daughter of Shuah.
This Confucian scholar-turned-revolutionary led rebel armies against French colonial forces in 19th-century Vietnam, refusing to surrender even after they desecrated his ancestral tombs. Who was he?
Phan Đình Phùng (1847 - January 21, 1896) was a Vietnamese revolutionary who led rebel armies against French colonial forces in Vietnam.
Born in 1988, this Indian politician served as an MLA from Delhi's Rajinder Nagar before joining the Rajya Sabha in 2022 and later switching parties to the BJP — who is he?
Raghav Chadha (born 11 November 1988) is an Indian politician and chartered accountant who serves as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha since 2022.

Rising to major general by 1979, this South Korean army officer backed his military academy friend's coup that year and later became, in 1987, the first president chosen by direct popular vote. Who is he?
Roh Tae-woo (4 December 1932 - 26 October 2021) was a South Korean army general and politician who served as the sixth president of South Korea from 1988 to 1993.

This Indian politician served as governor of five different states — including Jammu and Kashmir — after earlier representing Aligarh in the national parliament as a member of the Janata Dal. Who is he?

A close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and a founding member of the Jamia Millia Islamia university, this Hyderabad-born educationist rose to serve as president of India from 1967 until his death two years later — who was he?

Zakir Husain (8 February 1897 - 3 May 1969) was an Indian educationist and politician who served as the vice president of India from 1962 to 1967 and president of India from 13 May 1967 until his death on 3 May 1969.

Christian X: King of Denmark (1912–1947) and Iceland (1918–1944)

He served twice as France's prime minister and ran Paris as mayor for nearly two decades before finally winning the presidency in 1995. Which French statesman?
Jacques Chirac: President of France from 1995 to 2007.

Lutheranism: Major branch of Protestantism. The Lutheran churches adhere to the Bible and the ecumenical creeds, with Lutheran doctrine being explicated in the Book of Concord.

Manmohan Singh: Prime Minister of India from 2004 to 2014. A member of the Indian National Congress, Singh was the first and remains the only Sikh prime minister of India.
Built on the 19th-century work of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, which philosophy uses a 'base and superstructure' model and treats class struggle as the engine of historical change?
Marxism: Political philosophy. Marxism stands as one of the most influential and controversial intellectual traditions in modern history.

Mexican–American War: 1846–1848 conflict between Mexico and the United States.
A metallurgical engineer and Muslim Brotherhood figure, he became Egypt's 5th president in 2012 only to be ousted a year later in a coup led by General el-Sisi — who was he?
Mohamed Morsi: President of Egypt from 2012 to 2013.

Myanmar civil war (2021–present): Ongoing armed conflict in Southeast Asia.
This French jurist served as Minister of Justice under Édouard Philippe before becoming Minister of National Education in Gabriel Attal's 2024 government — who is she?

Qin Shi Huang: Emperor of China from 221 to 210 BC.

What is the atomic number of Bromine?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
In what year did Galileo Galilei die?
Galileo Galilei: Galileo has been called the father of observational astronomy, modern-era classical physics, the scientific method, and modern science.
In what year was Lithium discovered?
Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".
Which country is Dassault Falcon 900 from?
Dassault Falcon 900: France. The Dassault Falcon 900, commonly abbreviated as the F900, is a French-built corporate trijet aircraft made by Dassault Aviation.
Who is credited with discovering Antlia?
Antlia: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Antlia (from Ancient Greek ἀντλία) is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Factitious disorder imposed on another?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: Roy Meadow. The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
Who is credited with discovering Trisomy 18?
Trisomy 18: John H. Edwards. Trisomy 18, also known as Edwards syndrome, is a genetic disorder.
Who is credited with discovering Strontium?
Strontium: William Cruickshank. Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.

While working at a Soviet computing centre in 1985, this engineer created one of history's most popular video games — yet earned no royalties from it until founding a company with Henk Rogers in 1996. Who is he?
Alexey Pajitnov (born April 16, 1955) is a Russian and American computer engineer and video game designer.
This joint region where the foot meets the leg comprises three joints built from the talus, tibia, and fibula, enabling the foot's up-and-down flexing motions — what body part is it?
Ankle is the area where the foot and the leg meet.

Explicitly describing the relativity of motion and, by his own account, 23 years old in 499 CE, this figure is considered the first of the great mathematician-astronomers of classical Indian science — who is he?
Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was the first of the major mathematician-astronomers and early physicist from the classical age of Indian mathematics and Indian astronomy.
Causing frequent urination and a weak stream, this noncancerous enlargement of a male gland isn't caused by poor hygiene and has no known cure, only symptom management. What condition is it?
Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland.
What hydrated mineral salt of sodium, mined economically in only a few places worldwide, forms a white crystalline solid that can be dehydrated by heating?
Borax (also referred to as sodium borate, tincal and tincar) is a salt (ionic compound) normally encountered as a hydrated borate of sodium, with the chemical formula Na2H20B4O17.
Atomic number 20 and chemically akin to strontium and barium, this metal is the most common ingredient in limestone — found there as its carbonate. What element?
Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
This set of metabolic reactions oxidizes biological fuels using an electron acceptor like oxygen to produce ATP, the molecule that stores usable chemical energy in cells — what is it?

Cellular respiration is the process of oxidizing biological fuels using an inorganic electron acceptor, such as oxygen, to drive production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which stores chemical energy in a biologically accessible form.

This genus of flowering trees and shrubs, native to South and East Asia, Melanesia, and Australia, gave rise through extensive hybridization to oranges, lemons, grapefruits, and limes — what's the genus called?
Citrus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs in the family Rutaceae.
A genus of over 260 fungi, most of them parasites that bore into insects and other arthropods, this 'club-headed' organism has 1,500 years of use in Chinese medicine — what is it?
Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

Known by names ranging from the clinical to the crude to the childish — 'number two', 'dropping a deuce', 'doo-doo' — this basic biological process expels solid waste from the digestive tract. Name the process?

Defecation (or defaecation) follows digestion and is the necessary biological process by which organisms eliminate a solid, semisolid, or liquid waste material known as feces (or faeces) from the digestive tract via the anus or cloaca.

Massive enough to be rounded by its own gravity but too small to clear its orbital neighborhood like the solar system's eight major planets, Pluto became the prototype of this category after a 2006 reclassification. Name the category?

Dwarf planet is a small planetary-mass object that is in direct orbit around the Sun, massive enough to be gravitationally rounded, but insufficient to achieve orbital dominance like the eight classical planets of the Solar System.
This tightly coiled duct sits behind each testicle, serving as the crucial link to the vas deferens where sperm mature before their onward journey — what is it?
Epididymis (pl.: epididymides or) is an elongated tubular genital organ attached to the posterior side of each one of the two male reproductive glands, the testicles.
Which group of vascular plants, which reproduce via spores rather than seeds or flowers, are known for their large megaphyll leaves and the coiled 'fiddleheads' many species unfurl as new growth?
Fern (Polypodiopsida or Polypodiophyta) are a group of vascular plants (land plants with vascular tissues such as xylem and phloem) that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
Reclassified twice before settling into its own genus, this Gram-variable, non-spore-forming coccobacillus is barely one to 1.5 micrometers across — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
A friar, mathematician, and meteorologist who quietly worked out the laws of heredity with garden peas — and only got credit long after his death — who was this founder of genetics?
Gregor Mendel (20 July 1822 - 6 January 1884) was an Austrian biologist, meteorologist, mathematician, Augustinian friar and abbot of St.
This discipline governs the design and formal description ('blazon') of coats of arms, crests, and other armorial bearings — what is it called?
Heraldry (also known as armoury) is a discipline relating to the design, display, study and transmission of armorial bearings.
A person with this condition is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness, alarmed by even the most minor symptom — what is it?

Hypochondriasis is a condition in which a person is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness. International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10) classifies hypochondriasis as a mental and behavioral disorder.
Widely planted outside its native South America for its striking purple flowers, this tree is considered Vulnerable in the wild according to the IUCN — which species?
Jacaranda mimosifolia is a sub-tropical tree native to south-central South America that has been widely planted elsewhere because of its attractive and long-lasting violet-colored flowers.

This 20th-century Peruvian writer of mestizo descent composed novels, poems, and stories in both Spanish and Quechua, and even coined a new literary idiom to render Indigenous perspective more authentically — who is he?
José María Arguedas (Spanish) was a Peruvian novelist, poet, and anthropologist.
Which aromatic Mediterranean evergreen tree, prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture and used to season food, can grow up to 20 meters tall with smooth, glossy leaves?
Laurus nobilis is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves.

This American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft is a comprehensive update of an older Cold War-era design, and remains the only version of its lineage still in production, with 500 delivered to 26 operators. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules is a medium-size American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
Often found combined with iron in minerals, this hard, brittle, silvery transition metal is added to stainless steel to improve strength and wear resistance. What element is it (symbol Mn)?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
This field of study examines and evaluates the procedures researchers use to gather and interpret data, rather than the findings those procedures produce — what is it called?
Methodology is the study of research methods.
First documented with ice cream and water by a Tanzanian student and his professor in the 1960s, this contested observation says warmer liquids can outrace colder ones to freezing — what's it called?
Mpemba effect is the observation that very hot liquids or colloids (such as ice cream) can freeze more quickly than colder ones, for similar volumes and surrounding conditions.

Discovered in a fossil-rich West African formation and first described in 1976 but not formally named until 1999, this rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur lived roughly 115 to 105 million years ago — which genus?
Nigersaurus is a genus of rebbachisaurid sauropod dinosaur that lived during the middle Cretaceous period, about 115 to 105 million years ago.
Chemists still debate the exact definition, but generally, any large molecule containing a carbon-hydrogen or carbon-carbon bond falls into this broad class of compounds. What is it?
Organic compound are a subclass of chemical compounds of carbon.
Made by grinding dry-roasted legumes and often tweaked with salt or emulsifiers, this protein-rich spread is the most popular of all the nut butters — what is it?
Peanut butter is a food paste or spread made from ground, dry-roasted peanuts.
Someone who specializes in matter, motion, and force through space and time earns the title 'physicist' — so what is the field they devote themselves to?
Physics is the scientific study of matter, its fundamental constituents, its motion and behavior through space and time, and the related entities of energy and force.
Which compound pulls double duty as a dietary iodine supplement and as the pill that protects the thyroid gland during radiation emergencies?
Potassium iodide (KI) is a chemical compound, medication, and dietary supplement.
A polyphenol from the flavonoid family with a naturally bitter taste, this compound turns up in capers and red onions and gets added to supplements — what is it?
Quercetin is a plant flavonol from the flavonoid group of polyphenols.
Holding a professorship in biology, neurology, and neurosurgery at Stanford, this primatologist is also a research associate with Kenya's National Museums — who is he?
Robert Sapolsky (born April 6, 1957) is an American academic, neuroscientist, and primatologist.
Which genus of large, tropical, many-legged predators takes its name from ancient Greek words meaning roughly 'thorn' and 'earthworm'?
Scolopendra (from Ancient Greek (sklops), meaning "thorn", and (nteron), meaning "earthworm") is a species-rich genus of large tropical centipedes of the family Scolopendridae.
Typically a bony enclosure around a vertebrate's brain, though cartilage in some fish and amphibians, this head structure combines a neurocranium with a facial skeleton — name it?

Skull is typically a bony enclosure around the brain of a vertebrate. In a human, the skull comprises two prominent parts: the neurocranium and the facial skeleton, which evolved from the first pharyngeal arch.
Often caused by a lesion narrowing an artery, as in atherosclerosis, this condition is sometimes also called a stricture or coarctation — what is it?
Stenosis (from Ancient Greek (stens) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.

A carnivorous marsupial formerly found across mainland Australia but now confined to Tasmania, this animal became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial after the thylacine's extinction in 1936. What is this fierce creature?
Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.
Tetrapods have these digits at the end of each limb; horses walk on their very tips in what's called an unguligrade stance — what are they?
Toe are the digits of the foot of a tetrapod.

This membrane-bound organelle, found in plant and fungal cells and some others, is essentially a water-filled storage compartment with no fixed shape, formed when smaller membrane vesicles fuse together. What is it called?
Vacuole is a membrane-bound organelle which is present in plant and fungal cells and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.

Dubbed the "father of English geology," this man created the first detailed geological map of an entire country — yet his humble background got him snubbed by scientists and even landed him in debtors' prison. Who was he?
William Smith (geologist) (23 March 1769 - 28 August 1839) was an English geologist, credited with creating the first detailed, nationwide geological map of any country.
Also known by his Latinized name Rhazes, this Persian polymath authored over 200 manuscripts on medicine, philosophy, and astronomy during the Islamic Golden Age — who was he?
Abu Bakr al-Razi: 10th-century Iranian physician and polymath.
Based on a civilian widebody jet, this European aerial-refueling tanker holds over 90% of the air-to-air refueling market outside the United States, with 17 countries as customers — which aircraft?

Airbus A330 MRTT: Aerial refuelling tanker aircraft. The Airbus A330 Multi Role Tanker Transport (MRTT) is a European aerial refueling and military transport aircraft based on the civilian Airbus A330.
Known in mineral form as gibbsite, this amphoteric white compound with the formula Al(OH)3 is a major component of the ore bauxite — what is it?
Aluminium hydroxide: Chemical compound. Aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric, meaning it has both basic and acidic properties.
Named for a 19th-century Swedish physicist and symbolized by a letter of the Swedish alphabet, which unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a metre, handy for measuring atoms and bond lengths?
Angstrom: Unit of length. The unit is named after the Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström (1814–1874).
Its name comes from Greek roots meaning 'chief' and 'creator,' and historians often identify whole vanished civilizations by what survives of this visual art. What is it?
Architecture: Art and technique of designing buildings.
This medical term describes the partial or complete wasting away of a body part due to poor nourishment, nerve loss, or disuse — what is the condition called?
Atrophy: Partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body. A diminished muscular trophic condition is designated as atrophy.
In continuous production since 1974 — the longest run of any civilian turboprop plane in its class — this twin-engine model also serves in medevac and flight-inspection roles — what is it?
Beechcraft Super King Air: Light twin-turboprop transport aircraft family.
This flowering vine's dried fruit is one of the most commonly traded spices in the world, its heat coming from a compound called piperine — what plant?
Black pepper: Ground fruit of the family Piperaceae.
Distinguished by a cube-shaped body, this class of stinging cnidarians includes species such as Chironex fleckeri, whose venom is often fatal to humans — what is it?
Box jellyfish: Class of cnidarians distinguished by their cube-shaped medusae.
Developed in 1964 at Britain's Royal Radar Establishment and influenced by JOVIAL, this programming language was chosen by the UK Ministry of Defence in 1971 for military applications — what is it?
CORAL: Early programming language. The R was originally for "radar", not "real-time".
Derived from Greek words for 'heart' and 'study,' this branch of internal medicine covers coronary artery disease, heart failure, and electrophysiology — which medical field?
Cardiology: Branch of medicine dealing with the heart.
Triggered by anything from a stroke to a bout of altitude sickness, this dangerous buildup of fluid inside the skull raises pressure on brain tissue and can cause seizures or worse — what is it?
Cerebral edema: Excess accumulation of fluid in the brain.
Every animal in this group shares five telltale traits — including a notochord, pharyngeal slits, and a tail that extends past the anus — at some stage of life; which of these belongs to that phylum?
Chordate: Phylum of animals having a dorsal nerve cord.
This genus of demersal fish, named by Linnaeus in 1758, includes an Atlantic and a Pacific species prized for their mild flavor and flaky white flesh — what fish is it?
Cod: Common name for several fish, but mainly the demersal genus Gadus.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.

With nearly 24,000 ommatidia in each compound eye and wings usually held flat rather than folded, this iridescent flying insect is often confused with its lighter-bodied damselfly cousins — what is it?
Named for the large trunk-like proboscis of its males, this giant oceangoing pinniped can weigh up to 4,000 kilograms and was once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil. What animal is it?
Elephant seal: Genus of aquatic carnivores.
Sold under the brand name Nexium, this proton pump inhibitor treats acid reflux by blocking an enzyme in the stomach's acid-producing cells — what is it?
Esomeprazole: Medication which reduces stomach acid.
While its deciduous neighbors drop everything and go bare for winter, this kind of plant keeps its foliage green and working all year round — what's the botanical term?
Evergreen: Plant that has leaves in all seasons.

Modern phylogenetics calls this a paraphyletic group covering nearly every vertebrate except the tetrapods — gill-bearing, limbless-of-digits, and usually cold-blooded. What aquatic animals are these?
This mathematical principle links differentiation and integration, showing the two operations to be essentially inverses of each other — what is it called?
Fundamental theorem of calculus: Relationship between derivatives and integrals.
The longest member of the weasel family at up to 1.8 meters, this noisy, highly social river-dweller lives in family groups along the Amazon and in the Pantanal — which animal?
With a black head, white cheeks and yellow underparts, this widespread European songbird was split from two Asian relatives after 2005 DNA studies?
Great tit: Passerine bird in the tit family Paridae.

Nicknamed the 'Halloween beetle' in North America for invading homes each October to overwinter, this extremely color-variable insect was introduced there from eastern Asia to control aphids — what species is it?
Harmonia axyridis: Species of beetle. Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.
The offspring of a stallion and a female donkey, this equine hybrid is the rarer reciprocal cross to the mule and was often mistaken in European folklore for a horse-cow hybrid — what is it?
Hinny: Domestic horse–donkey hybrid. It is the reciprocal cross to the more common mule, which is the product of a male donkey (a jack) and a female horse (a mare).
First made in Belgium in 1956 and sold under the brand names Atarax and Vistaril, this first-generation antihistamine also treats anxiety and insomnia — what drug?
Hydroxyzine: Antihistamine drug. It is used in the treatment of itchiness, anxiety, insomnia, and nausea (including that due to motion sickness).
Symbolized by the '∞' sign and debated by philosophers since ancient Greece, this endless concept was later shown by Georg Cantor to come in different sizes when applied to sets. What is it?
Infinity: Mathematical concept. Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Fluent in Quechua after being raised in two Indigenous households as a child, this Peruvian novelist and anthropologist became known for his intimate portrayals of Andean culture — who is he?
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
Marked by weariness and a desire to act without the energy to do so, which condition can be a normal response to poor sleep or stress, or a sign of underlying illness?
Lethargy: State of tiredness, weariness, fatigue, or lack of energy.
Predominantly black and white with pink and grey highlights, this small Eurasian bird forms social flocks of six to seventeen outside breeding season and often nests in thorny scrub. What is it?
Long-tailed tit: Species of bird in Europe and Asia.

Discovered in 2005 by the same Palomar team whose haul of big, icy Kuiper-belt bodies pushed astronomers to demote Pluto in 2006, this fourth-largest dwarf planet has a methane-frosted, tholin-reddened surface — what is it?
Makemake: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Distinguished by its darker camouflage, conformal fuel tanks, and a two-seat cockpit, this all-weather multirole fighter first flew in 1986 for long-range interdiction missions — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle: American all-weather multirole fighter aircraft.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
Also called flystrike, this parasitic condition occurs when fly larvae infest and feed on the tissue of a living animal — what is it?
An oily alkaloid from nightshade plants like tobacco, it doubles as a potent insect neurotoxin and once served as an insecticide, inspiring the neonicotinoid pesticides — what is it?
Nicotine: Chemical stimulant produced by some plants.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?
Its name comes from the Greek for 'making,' and it leans on devices like assonance, alliteration, and metre to evoke meanings beyond the literal — what literary art is this?
Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.
Discovered in 1861 via flame spectroscopy by Bunsen and Kirchhoff, this alkali metal is named from the Latin word for 'deep red' — which element?
Rubidium: Chemical element with atomic number 37 (Rb)
This large, rainbow-plumed parrot native to the forests of Central and South America is the national bird of Honduras — what is it?
Scarlet macaw: Species of bird. Like its relative the blue-and-yellow macaw, the scarlet macaw is a popular bird in aviculture as a result of its striking plumage.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
Built from four fused carbon rings, this class of organic compounds includes cholesterol, testosterone, and anabolic performance-enhancers — what is it called?
Steroid: Polycyclic organic compound having sterane as a core structure.
Native to the Balkan Peninsula, this fragrant flowering shrub in the olive family is cultivated widely across Europe and North America for its clusters of purple or white blooms — which species?
Syringa vulgaris: Plant species in the olive family.
Found in pufferfish, blue-ringed octopuses, and rough-skinned newts, this potent sodium-channel-blocking neurotoxin is also being trialed as a treatment for cancer-related pain — what is it?
Tetrodotoxin: Neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Nocturnal and tree-dwelling, this lizard species is native to Asia and various Pacific Islands — which reptile is it?
Tokay gecko: Species of reptile. The tokay gecko (Gekko gecko) is a nocturnal arboreal gecko in the genus Gekko, the true geckos.
Carrying the NATO nickname 'Backfire,' this supersonic Soviet bomber with variable-sweep wings first dropped conventional bombs during the Soviet–Afghan War — which aircraft is it?
Tupolev Tu-22M: Russian long-range supersonic strategic bomber.
Born in 1946, this German facilitator and non-fiction writer built a career exploring esoteric subjects until her death in 2011 — who was she?
Vera F. Birkenbihl: German facilitator, writer. Vera Felicitas Birkenbihl (26 April 1946 - 3 December 2011) was a German facilitator, non-fiction writer, and esoteric.
First isolated in 1669 by alchemist Henning Brand, this waxy, translucent form of an element glows faintly green in the dark and ignites spontaneously in air — which substance?
Tracing its formal origins to Aristotle and later shaped by Carl Linnaeus, this branch of biology studies the structure, classification and behavior of animals — which field?
The symbol for hassium is Hs. Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
The symbol for actinium is Ac. Actinium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ac and atomic number 89.

Catherine Zeta-Jones (born 25 September 1969) is a Welsh actress.

Ji Chang-wook: Ji Chang-wook (Korean: 지창욱; born 5 July 1987) is a South Korean actor and singer.
In what year did Farrah Fawcett die?
Farrah Fawcett: Mary Ferrah Leni "Farrah" Fawcett (February 2, 1947 – June 25, 2009) was an American actress.
